audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Joshua / Yehoshua Achan, Ai defeat, lot exposure, confession, and Valley of Achor execution narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for corporate trespass, failed attack, thirty-six deaths, Joshua's lament, lot-based identification, Achan's confession, concealed plunder, execution of household and animals, stone heap, and collective-punishment concerns.

verses.restored: Children of Israel acted unfaithfully concerning devoted thing: Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from tribe of Judah, took from devoted thing; and anger of YHWH burned against children of Israel.

familiar.text: But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel.

verses.restored: Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and spoke to them, saying, Go up and spy out land. The men went up and spied out Ai.

familiar.text: And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Bethaven, on the east side of Bethel, and spake unto them, saying, Go up and view the country.  And the men went up and viewed Ai.

verses.restored: They returned to Joshua and said to him, Let not all people go up; about two thousand or three thousand men may go up and strike Ai. Do not weary all people there, for they are few.

familiar.text: And they returned to Joshua, and said unto him, Let not all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai; and make not all the people to labour thither; for they are but few.

verses.restored: So from people about three thousand men went up there, and they fled before men of Ai.

familiar.text: So there went up thither of the people about three thousand men: and they fled before the men of Ai.

verses.restored: Men of Ai struck from them about thirty-six men and pursued them before gate as far as Shebarim and struck them on descent; heart of people melted and became as water.

familiar.text: And the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men: for they chased them from before the gate even unto Shebarim, and smote them in the going down: wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water.

verses.restored: Joshua tore his garments and fell upon his face to earth before ark of YHWH until evening, he and elders of Israel, and they put dust upon their heads.

familiar.text: And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the LORD until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads.

familiar.text: And Joshua said, Alas, O LORD God, wherefore hast thou at all brought this people over Jordan, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? would to God we had been content, and dwelt on the other side Jordan!

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Joshua, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou thus upon thy face?

verses.restored: Israel has sinned/misaligned, and they also crossed my covenant that I commanded them; they took from devoted thing, and also stole, and also deceived, and also put it among their own vessels.

familiar.text: Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.

familiar.text: Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.

familiar.text: And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.

familiar.text: And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones.

verses.restored: They raised over him a great heap of stones, to this day; and YHWH turned from burning of his anger. Therefore name of that place is called Valley of Achor/Trouble to this day.

familiar.text: And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day. So the LORD turned from the fierceness of his anger. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.

translation_notes: The narrative opens by assigning one person's act to all Israel, demonstrating a strong corporate-responsibility model.
The failed attack was launched on scouts' confidence with no recorded inquiry of YHWH, and thirty-six soldiers die before the hidden theft is identified.
The lot process narrows tribe, clan, household, and individual, but the text does not explain its mechanics or provide modern evidentiary safeguards.
Achan confesses taking a Shinar mantle, silver, and gold from Jericho's devoted spoil. His confession does not ethically justify punishment of uninvolved relatives.

Verse 24 explicitly brings Achan's sons, daughters, animals, tent, and possessions to the execution site. Verse 25 shifts between singular and plural, strongly suggesting the household and animals were destroyed with him, though interpreters debate details.
The killing of children and animals for one adult's theft is collective punishment and must be categorically rejected as modern justice.
The community that executed Jericho now punishes private appropriation of sacred-war plunder; this internal consistency does not make the larger herem system ethical.
Achor wordplay links Achan's troubling of Israel to the valley's name and later prophetic traditions of hope require separate cross-reference.
safety_note: Never use Joshua 7 to justify collective punishment, execution of children, destruction of families, trial by lot, coercive confession, killing for theft, or leader-controlled purges. Center transparent accountability, individual responsibility, reliable evidence, restitution where possible, and categorical protection of relatives, dependents, and animals from another person's wrongdoing.
